question: In proptosis evaluation, the direction of globe displacement (axial vs non-axial) helps localise the orbital lesion because intraconal masses produce axial (straight forward) proptosis while extraconal masses displace the globe away from the lesion.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and represents a key clinical localisation principle. Axial proptosis = intraconal lesion (muscle cone mass compresses the globe forward uniformly). Non-axial proptosis (globe displaced away from the lesion) = extraconal lesion. For example, a superolateral lacrimal gland tumour produces inferomedial globe displacement — the globe 'runs away' from the mass.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Intraconal lesions (within the muscle cone, e.g. optic nerve glioma, cavernous haemangioma) push the globe directly forward — pure axial proptosis — because they expand within the cone. Extraconal lesions (e.g. lacrimal gland tumours superolaterally, ethmoidal mucoceles medially) displace the globe away from the mass: a lacrimal gland tumour displaces the eye inferomedially, a medial wall mucocele displaces it laterally.
